automation_name: AI Security Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.rule: Only records with a visible, precise publication or update timestamp strictly inside this two-day collection window were retained.

searched_topics: agent and tool security including MCP, plugins, browsers, delegated authority, and autonomous action
identity, authentication, authorization, credentials, and least privilege
model, dataset, dependency, artifact, runtime, cloud, hardware, and deployment supply chains
threat modeling, red teaming, security evaluation, assurance, monitoring, and release gates
AI security standards, regulation, governance, audit evidence, and risk management
public AI security incidents, mitigations, patches, disclosures, and lessons learned
source_method: Public-web discovery followed by NVD CVE API keyword/date query and CVE Services API record retrieval; product advisories, commits, and releases are linked where the public CVE record references them.

local_context_checked.duplicate_check: Searched local raw, raw/processed, and docs/wiki for identifiers; CVE-2026-116575 was already captured in the 2026-10-26 processed collector artifact and is excluded.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Services public record referencing Patchstack's public plugin advisory; corroborated by NVD.
qualifying_findings.summary: AI Engine for WordPress through 3.8.6 has a missing-authorization flaw described as incorrectly configured access-control security levels.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Meow Apps AI Engine WordPress plugin through 3.8.6; media/object access-control boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI application integrations that expose media or model-adjacent content need object-level authorization rather than relying on route reachability.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: AI Engine product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain only the local access-control implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Confirm Patchstack's affected-object details and a maintainer-fixed release before synthesis.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Services public record referencing the CERT-In public vulnerability note; corroborated by NVD.
qualifying_findings.summary: CreditNirvana Agentic AI Call Centre exposes a static API key in a client-side JavaScript bundle; an unauthenticated remote actor can extract it and use the application API to retrieve call transcripts and recordings.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: CreditNirvana Agentic AI Call Centre; client bundle to API credential boundary; no fixed version stated in the CVE record.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Voice-agent deployments must not distribute reusable provider or application credentials to browsers, especially where APIs expose conversation data.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the credential-exposure and call-data privacy implication locally.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Recheck CERT-In for remediation, rotation guidance, affected versions, and any incident disclosure.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Services public record referencing a Turkish national cybersecurity public advisory; corroborated by NVD.
qualifying_findings.summary: Keepnet Labs Agentic AI / Agentic Ally has an authentication-bypass vulnerability before commit 0ef61f2e.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Keepnet Agentic AI / Agentic Ally before 0ef61f2e; authentication boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Identity enforcement is a prerequisite for constraining delegated agent actions and access to connected tools or data.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local authentication-control implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Inspect the advisory and repository history for attack preconditions, release mapping, and a supported fixed build.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Services public record with linked repository source and fix commit; corroborated by NVD.
qualifying_findings.summary: The ai-sdlc plugin MCP server through 0.31.2 interpolates a repo argument into gh commands via execSync(), enabling OS command injection through shell metacharacters; the CVE explicitly identifies prompt-injected agents as a route to execution.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: ai-sdlc plugin MCP server through 0.31.2; check-issue/check-pr-status repository argument to local shell boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent-controlled tool arguments must be structured and passed without a shell; prompt injection can otherwise cross directly into the MCP server user's authority.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: General ai-sdlc tooling belongs in ai-wiki and development workflow practice in ai-dev-wiki; retain this MCP execution-boundary security finding locally.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Verify the first released fixed plugin version and whether deployments need credential rotation after exposure.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: MLflow's public GitHub Security Advisory, linked fix/release, and CVE Services record.
qualifying_findings.summary: MLflow 3.10.0 through 3.17.0 permits schemeless relative prompt sources in model-version creation, allowing a remote caller to set a server-local artifact path and read files through the model-version artifact API; fixed in 3.17.0.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: MLflow 3.10.0 to 3.17.0; prompt model-version source validation and server-local artifact read boundary; fixed in 3.17.0.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Prompt and model registries are artifact boundaries: path validation must prevent callers from turning model metadata into host-file reads.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: MLflow product background belongs in ai-wiki; retain the prompt-artifact path-validation control locally.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 3.17.0 and audit model-version sources plus exposed MLflow server authentication.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: MLflow's public GitHub Security Advisory, linked fix/release, and CVE Services record.
qualifying_findings.summary: MLflow CrewAI autologging 2.19.0 through 3.17.0 can stringify credential-bearing nested agent values and send plaintext provider API keys to the MLflow trace backend or OTLP destination; fixed in 3.17.0.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: MLflow 2.19.0 to 3.17.0; CrewAI autologging to trace/OTLP observability boundary; fixed in 3.17.0.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Observability pipelines must treat agent objects as sensitive input and redact provider credentials before spans are persisted or exported.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: MLflow and CrewAI product background belong in ai-wiki; retain the trace-secret handling implication locally.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 3.17.0, rotate potentially exported keys, and restrict trace-reader access.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: MLflow's public GitHub Security Advisory, linked fix/release, and CVE Services record.
qualifying_findings.summary: MLflow 3.12.0rc0 through 3.17.0 accepts request-selected descendants beneath third-party scorer allowed modules, allowing artifact-uploaded Python code to be imported and instantiated through scorer invocation when the package is writable; fixed in 3.17.0.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: MLflow 3.12.0rc0 to 3.17.0; GenAI scorer module allowlist, artifact upload, and Python import boundary; fixed in 3.17.0.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Evaluation and scorer plug-ins are executable supply-chain components; namespace-prefix allowlists are insufficient where artifacts can write under approved packages.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: MLflow product background belongs in ai-wiki; retain the evaluator plug-in supply-chain and runtime-execution implication locally.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 3.17.0, review scorer packages and writable artifact paths, and restrict experiment/run creation rights.

confidence_notes: All retained items have precise public CVE publication timestamps within the window.
The MLflow findings have maintainer-authored GitHub advisories, fix commits, and a named fixed release, yielding high confidence.
The AI Engine and Keepnet records need detailed maintainer or advisory reconciliation before durable synthesis because the CVE summaries provide limited remediation detail.
follow_up_actions: During ingestion, keep each MLflow vulnerability as a separate security boundary even though all are fixed in 3.17.0.
Recheck product advisories for fixed releases, affected versions, and deployment guidance for AI Engine, CreditNirvana, and Keepnet.
Do not synthesize broad product background locally; route it to ai-wiki or ai-dev-wiki under federation rules.
